findings.passage: And this act would federalize the elections.
findings.note: In a recorded interview (transcript from On the Record), he describes the SAVE Act's effects on registration and tribal ID. Passage below is the ID-related one; see next finding for the rest.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register (SAVE Act)

findings.passage: Uh very very uh difficult for tribal members to vote because of the act says it you have to have an expiration date on your ID.
findings.note: He says the SAVE Act's ID rule, which he describes as requiring an expiration date, would make voting hard for tribal members, whose tribal ID has none.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register (SAVE Act)

findings.passage: They would purge names off the off the registration rolls, and people would have to reapply, and they couldn't even get re-registered to vote using their birth certificate.
findings.note: He describes the SAVE Act as removing names from registration rolls and requiring people to re-register, including married women whose names differ from their birth certificates.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register (SAVE Act)

findings.passage: And that act, which he frames as stopping non-citizens from voting, it's actually about stopping citizens from voting.

subjects: proof of citizenship to register (SAVE Act)

findings.passage: It's not about non-citizens voting.

subjects: proof of citizenship to register (SAVE Act)

findings.passage: It's about stopping citizens from voting who are members of tribes, who are college students, who are women, or who dwell in cities.

findings.passage: But vote by mail stops all those shenanigans.

findings.passage: Oregon initiated it and in my For the People Act, which was Senate Bill number one a couple years ago that we came close to passing but unfortunately didn't, that bill would have allowed or actually required vote by mail opportunity for everyone in America cuz that's the top gold standard high integrity system.
